title: dedicated-fleet-autoscaler-burst-controls-util-reporting-v26
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds burst token-bucket controls and new fleet utilization metrics for Dedicated. Backwards-compatible config; operators can opt-in. Improves autoscaler responsiveness and adds per-fleet throughput guarantees.
description: This PR implements burst controls and richer utilization reporting for the Dedicated fleet autoscaler. Motivation: customers running bursty workloads (cron jobs, batch spikes) requested bounded short-term throughput without permanently increasing reserved capacity. Changes introduce a token-bucket based burst controller, a per-fleet throughput_guarantee config, and additional Prometheus metrics for observed and provisioned throughput. The description below summarizes the user-visible changes, implementation notes, migration path, and rollout plan. User-visible changes: 1) New autoscaler config fields: burst_window_seconds, burst_tokens, burst_refill_rate, and throughput_guarantee_rps. 2) Console: Autoscale config page shows burst budget and historical burst consumption graphs. 3) Metrics: dedicated_fleet_provisioned_rps, dedicated_fleet_observed_rps, dedicated_fleet_burst_budget_remaining, dedicated_fleet_burst_events_total. Implementation notes: - Implemented a light-weight token-bucket (burst_controller.go) that is consulted during scale-up decisions; it allows transient scale-ups up to burst_tokens while decrementing burst_budget and refilling at burst_refill_rate. - The autoscaler policy now evaluates both utilization and burst budget; when burst_budget is sufficient, it permits short-lived replica increases without affecting long-term target capacity. - Added persistence of burst budget to the fleet state (small RGB key in redis with TTL) to survive controller restarts. - Extended metrics export and Grafana dashboards for SRE visibility. Benchmarks: on our perf-lab workloads this change reduces 99th pct latency for bursty traffic by ~22% and achieves required throughput spikes up to 2x baseline for up to configured burst_window without provisioning extra nodes. Migration path: configs default to existing behavior (burst disabled) so no operator action required. To enable, operators add the new fields to Dedicated fleet config or toggle via Console. Rollout plan: staged rollout starting with canary fleet (10% traffic) for one week, extended to 50% after smoke pass, full rollout after observing metrics and two incident-free weeks. Security/operational notes: rate limits still apply; burst does not bypass tenant quotas. See linked Linear ENG-2042 for follow-up smoothing heuristics.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can we ensure burst budget persistence is tolerant to Redis restarts? Suggest adding TTL and update-on-start logic.
Asha Patel (author): Added TTL and startup reconciliation in pkg/redis/burst_state.go; if state missing we reconstruct from configured max tokens.
Noah Kim (reviewer): Integration tests flaky in CI when simulating rapid bursts. Can we add retry/backoff?
Asha Patel (author): Adjusted integration test harness to use deterministic time source and added retry for controller reconcile; CI re-run is green.
Sofia Martinez (reviewer): UI copy nit: rename 'burst_tokens' to 'burst_budget' for clarity. Also request an e2e smoke for console changes.
Asha Patel (author): Renamed field in config and API (kept alias for backward compat). Added e2e smoke job for console.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Verified metrics and canary results in perf-lab; approving to merge after CI green and release notes added.
benchmark_summary: Perf-lab on r5-gpu nodes: median throughput unchanged; 95th pct latency improved 9%; 99th pct latency improved 22% for bursty traffic patterns. Sustained short bursts up to 2x baseline RPS for configured window without new node provisioning. Observability added to verify budget consumption and emergency fallback triggers.
rollout_plan: Canary 10% (1 week) -> 50% (3 days) -> full rollout after 2 incident-free weeks. Monitoring: dedicated_fleet_burst_events_total, dedicated_fleet_burst_budget_remaining, autoscaler_scale_events. Abort criteria: >1% error-rate regression or repeated emergency fallbacks in canary.
notes_for_ops: To enable bursts, update fleet config with throughput_guarantee_rps and burst settings. Default is disabled. Operators should monitor new metrics and set alerts for burst_budget_remaining < 10% and emergency_fallback_count > 0.
